notes: Kuhn's equation κλέος ἄφθιτον = śrávas ... ákṣitam; Watkins 1995 ch. 15 frame PRO(dat) + BE + IMPERISHABLE FAME. The dative 1st-person pronoun stands in both (Gk μοι sg., Ved. asmé pl.; singular follows Greek). The verb 'be' is Greek only (Ved. has dhehi): interpolated; the Greek future is rendered by the PIE subjunctive.

plan.english: Place imperishable fame on us for a lifetime!

notes: Watkins 1995 ch. 15: god as subject, PRO(dat) + *dʰeh₁- + *ḱléwos *n̥dʰgʷʰitom + *h₂oyu- (EVER). Ved. dhehi (RV 1.9.7, checked in VedaWeb) is the reduplicated present imperative *dʰe-dʰh₁-dʰí (> *dhazdhi, Av. dazdi), and Timocreon's τίθει is the present imperative of the same reduplicated stem, so the line has the present dʰedʰh₁dʰí (round 1 wrongly had the root aorist). *h₂óyu is root-level only (Ved. viśvā́yu- is a compound epithet, Gk αἰϝεί a locative of the stem), so it is not claimed secure; the locative h₂yéwi 'in (one's) lifetime' is interpolated. Krisa and Timocreon are quoted from Watkins/West, not in local corpora. Overlaps poetics-gifts-012 (same Vedic verse); this line's own evidence is Krisa αἰϝεί and Timocreon's κλέος … τίθει.

plan.english: He places imperishable fame upon himself.

notes: Watkins 1995 ch. 15: man as subject, PRO(nom) + *dʰeh₁- MIDDLE + imperishable fame. Ved. dhatte is the reduplicated present middle; Herodotus (quoted from West 2007 ch. 10) has the middle aorist of the same root; the present stem follows Vedic. Ved. ákṣiti- is the i-stem variant of the adjective; Il. 9.413 supplies the exact ἄφθιτος. The emphatic pronoun follows Ved. sá.

plan.english: May he hold imperishable fame for a lifetime.

notes: The Krisa votive verse (7th c., quoted from Watkins 1995 ch. 15; not in local corpora): '(that) he too may have imperishable fame forever'. The line stands only on the noun phrase *ḱléwos *n̥dʰgʷʰitom (RV 1.9.7 śrávaḥ … ákṣitam, checked); the frame is Greek only: *seǵʰ- (ἔχω, optative as in ἔχοι) is interpolated (Vedic expresses the frame with dhatte, see fame-003). *h₂óyu is a root-level match only (αἰϝεί : viśvā́yu-), not claimed secure; the locative h₂yéwi is interpolated.

máhi śrávaḥ = μέγα κλέος (West 2007 ch. 10; formula *méǵh₂ ḱléwos; RV 1.79.4, 1.43.7, Il. 6.446, Od. 2.125 checked locally). Ved. dhehi is the reduplicated present imperative (*dʰe-dʰh₁-dʰí > *dhazdhi, Av. dazdi), so the verb is the present dʰedʰh₁dʰí (round 1 had the aorist dʰh₁dʰí; review P6). The beneficiary dative stands in both (Ved. asmé, Gk αὐτῇ), but the Greek verb is renewed (ποιεῖτ(αι) 'makes for herself', Od. 2.126), so *dʰeh₁- is Vedic-only here and interpolated.

κλέος εὐρύ (Od. 3.83, 1.344) against Ved. urugāyám … śrávaḥ 'wide-going fame' (RV 6.65.6; all checked locally; West 2007 ch. 10, ch. 2 on renewal by pṛthú). Only *ḱléwos is secure: *h₁wérHus stands in the Vedic only as the first member urú- of the compound urugāyá- (root-level), so it is not claimed; no RV pāda has urú- with śrávas- (searched). The enclitic pronoun follows Ved. naḥ. The verb is Vedic only (Od. 3.83 has μετέρχομαι), interpolated; dhehi is the reduplicated present imperative, so the present dʰedʰh₁dʰí (round 1 had the aorist).

plan.english: We heard the fames of men.

notes: κλέα ἀνδρῶν 'the fames (famous deeds) of men' (Il. 9.524, Od. 8.73, checked). The shared element is the plural *ḱléwesh₂ 'famous deeds' with a genitive of the doer: Ved. táva śrávāṃsi 'your (Indra's) fames' as the subject of eulogy (RV 8.99.2, checked; also 3.30.5, 3.37.7; West 2007 ch. 1, ch. 10). The genitive *h₂nr̥ṓm is Greek only: West says the Vedic phrase śrávāṃsi narā́m 'cannot be documented', and in RV 1.43.7 nṛṇā́m goes with śatásya (round 1 misconstrued it; now support only). The Old Irish clothaib neirt (quoted from West; not in local corpora) is a different formation (*ḱlutom), support only. The verb 'hear' (*ḱlew-, figura etymologica) is interpolated: Greek has πεύθομαι; 1st plural as in the Greek.

'Seek fame' with the *sḱé-present of *h₂eys- 'seek' (*h₂is-sḱé-: Ved. iccha-, Slavic iskati): Ved. śrávaḥ icchámānaḥ (RV 1.126.1 of a king, 10.102.4; checked in VedaWeb, which writes ichámānaḥ) and the Lay of Igor's 'seek fame for yourselves' (West 2007 ch. 10; not in local corpora). The head, the verb stem, is secure; the object is not: Slavic slava is an o-grade derivative of *ḱlew- (root-level), so *ḱléwos is exact in Vedic only. Middle voice: Vedic has the middle participle, and the Russian has the reflexive dative 'for yourselves', i.e. seeking for oneself; the finite 3sg is interpolated (both texts have non-finite forms). Round 1 added 'the king' and 'goes forth' from other verses and pādas; both are dropped.

plan.english: May you place good fame on me.

notes: *h₁wésu ḱléwos 'good fame' (West 2007 ch. 10) in a request: Av. dāiiā̊ mē … vaŋhāuca srauuahi 'grant me … (in) good fame' (Y. 62.6, the prayer to Fire; checked in CAB, dāiiā̊ mē in 62.6a, srauuahi in 62.6c) and OIr fó chlú (Laws, quoted from West; not in local corpora). Il. 5.3 (κλέος ἐσθλόν, Greek renews the adjective) and Y. 30.10 (the same NP, used by poetics-gifts-013) are support only. Av. dā- continues *dʰeh₁- and *deh₃- alike, so the verb is interpolated (aorist optative of *dʰeh₁- 'place', as in the 'grant fame' frame). Avestan puts the fame in the locative; accusative object here.

plan.english: Now may I win good fame.

notes: Achilles' resolve (Il. 18.121) and Diomedes' (Il. 5.3), checked: win good fame in battle (West 2007 ch. 10 'Fame won in combat'). A pastiche, kept with that warning: the frame (*h₂er- 'win', aorist optative middle as in ἀροίμην) is Greek only and interpolated, and 'good' is secure only through Av. vohu (Y. 30.10, checked) and OIr fó (Laws, quoted from West, not in local corpora), passages without the verb; Greek renews the adjective (ἐσθλόν). nu follows Gk νῦν.

śrútyaṃ nā́ma = ὄνομα κλυτόν (RV 5.30.5, Od. 9.364, 19.183, checked; West 2007 ch. 10; Tocharian A ñom-klyu 'name-fame' as a compound). Only *h₁nómn̥ is secure. Greek κλυτός is exactly *ḱlutós, but Ved. śrútya- is a -ya- derivative of the root, so 'famous' is root-level and not claimed (no RV pāda has śrutá- with nā́man-; searched). 'Bears' follows Ved. bíbhrat (a participle there) and is interpolated.

Odysseus' false self-introduction 'to me (is) the famous name Aithon' (Od. 19.183, checked) against Indra 'famous by name' (RV 8.46.14, checked), West 2007 ch. 10. Weak: in the Vedic, nā́ma is adverbial ('by name') and śrútya- is a different derivative from κλυτός (root-level, not claimed), so only *h₁nómn̥ is secure; near-duplicate of fame-011. Dative of possession follows Greek; copula removed: the daughters have a nominal sentence at Od. 19.183 (ἐμοὶ δ' ὄνομα κλυτὸν Αἴθων, no verb; the treebank has an empty predicate), and RV 8.46.14 has the attributive accusative, also without a verb. In the Greek κλυτόν is attributive and the predicate is the name Αἴθων (no lexeme), so ḱlutós as predicate is the plan's, not the Greek's.

plan.english: He placed a name on the son.

notes: *h₁nómn̥ dʰeh₁- 'place a name' (West 2007 ch. 10): Hitt. lāman dāi- (ŠUM-an is the Sumerogram; dāiš is phonetic), Ved. nā́ma dhā-, Gk ὄνομα θέσθαι, Lat. nomen indere (in-dō < *dʰeh₁-). Hittite and Latin have the dative of the person named (-ši, mihi); 'the son' is interpolated (Appu names his son; the Greek name-givers are mother and grandfather). Aorist active follows Hittite preterite and Latin perfect; Greek has the middle.

Naming formula with the 3sg imperative of *h₁es- and a dative of the person: Hitt. ŠUM-an ēšdu 'let his name be (Bad)', Gk Ὀδυσεὺς ὄνομ' ἔστω 'let (his) name be Odysseus' (Autolycus naming his grandson). Both passages give a proper name; 'this' stands in for it and is interpolated.

The bahuvrihi *h₁su-ḱléwes- 'having good fame' (West 2007 ch. 10: Ved. suśrávas- = Gk εὐκλεής; Fortson §6.86): Ved. suśrávasam of Soma (RV 1.91.21) and of the people Dawn protects (RV 1.49.2), Homeric ἐϋκλεῖας predicated of men ('to be of good fame among the people', Od. 21.331); all checked locally. Same prefix, same s-stem second member, same adjective type in both branches; the engine's accent follows the Vedic (h₁suḱléwēs, Ved. suśrávas-). Support only: Av. haōsrauuaŋhəm 'good repute' (Yt. 10.58, 10.60, a noun; checked in CAB), the Vedic king's name Suśrávas- (RV 1.53.9, checked), OIr sochla 'renowned' and the names Εὐκλῆς, Illyr. Vescleves- (quoted from West; not in local corpora; Vescleves continues *h₁wesu-, not *h₁su-). Copula removed, as a noun phrase: the Vedic has the adjective attributively or as a noun, with no verb (RV 1.91.21 in a chain of epithets of Soma, RV 1.49.2 suśrávasaṃ jánam); the Greek does have a copula (Od. 21.331 οὔ πως ἔστιν ἐϋκλεῖας ... ἔμμεναι, an infinitive governed by ἔστιν 'it is possible', with a plural predicate). The Vedic is followed: two witnesses against one, and the older. The masculine gender is interpolated. The builder cannot credit a compound token as verified (its lex_id has no lexicon entry), so this line's secure_share is 0 although its one content word is the parallel itself.
